title: Reliability, Validity, and Preliminary Diagnostic Exploration of a Novel Dynamic Balance Test Tool
text: To investigate the reliability, validity, and exploratory diagnostic accuracy of a novel dynamic balance test tool (X-Balance Test, XBT). The reliability of XBT was assessed through test–retest assessments conducted both within a single day and across multiple days. Its validity was determined by examining the correlation between XBT and SEBT. Furthermore, the preliminary diagnostic exploration of XBT for evaluating lower extremity injury risk was calculated with the Star Excursion Balance Test as reference. The ICC for test–retest assessments ranges from 0.820 to 0.989, and the correlation coefficient for validity ranges from 0.495 to 0.770. The XBT demonstrated insufficient accuracy in diagnosing lower extremity injury risk (overall accuracy: 61.76%, sensitivity: 35.29%, specificity: 88.24%, positive likelihood ratio: 3.00, negative likelihood ratio: 0.33, positive predictive value: 75.00%, and negative predictive value: 57.69%). The XBT represents an alternative for measuring balance. However, the diagnostic findings on XBT were preliminary and exploratory.
